html:
SMTO-CFG-0042 — SMTO's model answer length setting is negative

GUID: eef09049-50a8-4652-aefc-5734ee8f91d1
Slug: config-llm-max-tokens-must-be-zero-or
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: cfg

What happened

  • A startup setting limits how long the AI model's answers can be, but it is set to a negative number, so SMTO stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the settings file (usually config.yaml) in a plain text editor and find max_tokens under the llm section. That line sets the longest answer the model may write.
  2. Change it to a positive number of tokens, or set it to 0 or delete the line to use SMTO's standard length. Then start SMTO again. Zero or no line means SMTO's standard allowance of 4,096 tokens; a negative length isn't possible.
  3. If SMTO is started by a script or service, ask its owner to check the AOR_LLM_MAX_TOKENS setting too; it must be 0 or more. That setting overrides the file, so a negative value there causes the same stop.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts and the startup screen reaches Ready.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details (or copy the message from the window where SMTO was started) and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change other limits or timeouts to work around this; only the answer length is wrong.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Configuration validation failed because llm.max_tokens (or AOR_LLM_MAX_TOKENS) is negative before product-profile output-token resolution.

What this means

  • Configured max_tokens is negative before product-profile output-token resolution. Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.

Why this can happen

  • Configured max_tokens is negative before product-profile output-token resolution.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the configured output-token field and its zero/default resolution rather than confusing it with total context size.

How to fix it

  • Set llm.max_tokens in the bootstrap YAML to 0 or a positive integer (0 resolves to the 4096-token product allowance), and check AOR_LLM_MAX_TOKENS, which overrides the file and is validated by Settings. Per-connection output allowances for new work are configured separately in Model routing; restart the Server after the change.
  • Set llm.max_tokens to a supported nonnegative value using the owning model configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported nonnegative configured value resolves to the intended output allowance.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Validation reports the owning configuration boundary; it does not change settings, migrate retained state or grant authority. Existing tasks retain their accepted snapshots unless the specific control explicitly supports a live change.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
